properties.chose: KEPT AS INTENT 2026-09-25 on Anthony's word. The need is settled — reflow2 maintains the link both ways, feeds results back across the distance, and says who can reach each artifact — and became req:the-design-knows-where-each-implementation-is, req:results-from-the-code-flow-back-into-a-design-that-lives-elsewhere and req:the-design-says-who-can-reach-each-artifact. The MECHANISM is not chosen: Claude Code recommended (b)+(c) — the design names each implementation once, and a machine matches its checkout to it — with out-of-tree measurement fixed first.
properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL (2026-09-25, from the dev_reflow2 hub session).

In Anthony's words: "my uncle, my sister, and myself can all collaborate on the design, but the implemented codebase for cure is on my local machine (we're basically already separating design from implementation). What probably needs to happen if we just make this separation permanent is that the design object still needs to know if and where is anything that is being implemented. that way, when I start implementing the cure design, the AI agent (you) can know exactly where the design requirements and constraints (within reflow2) and where the implementation is. This is a very important 'linkage' because the design object determines how it is implemented (and later on, when implemented design is being tested, feedback needs to be put back in the reflow2 design object)."

THE LINK HAS TWO DIRECTIONS: design → code (an agent starting from the design finds the implementation) and code → design (an agent working in the code finds its design; test results flow back into it).

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══
(a) EVERY ARTIFACT NAMES ITS REPOSITORY. Each registered file carries repository + path, and the commit it was measured at. Measuring it locally needs a map from repository to where it is checked out on this machine.
(b) THE DESIGN NAMES ITS IMPLEMENTATIONS ONCE. One record per implementation — repository, default branch, which part of the design it realizes — and artifacts are paths inside a named implementation. Where each is checked out is per machine and never in the design, the same principle as rule:a-design-is-named-by-an-id-not-a-path, applied to code.
(c) THE SESSION DECLARES IT. An agent opening a design from inside a checkout says "this checkout implements that design", and the server remembers it for that machine. Nothing new is stored in the design itself.
(b) and (c) compose: (b) is what the design knows; (c) is how one machine's checkout is matched to it.

FEEDBACK, THE RETURN LEG. Feeding a real run back already exists (a run fed back by file, with a converter from runner output). What separation adds is DISTANCE: results are produced where the code runs (a laptop, or the implementation repo's CI) and must reach wherever the design lives (a hosted design on flo2.io), authenticated. dec:idea-how-does-a-test-result-get-back-in-when-the-tester-may-not-be-an-agent is the open question about what makes it fire.
properties.name: A design apart from its code keeps the link to where it is implemented, takes results back, and says who can reach what
properties.rationale:
WHY IT MATTERS, beyond convenience: the design determines how the code is written and the test results judge the design. Without the link, separating them turns reflow2 back into documentation — accurate on the day it was written and unconnected afterwards.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, measured by search 2026-09-25:
· The server already knows a session's worktree and branch, and measures implementation facts against that worktree (req:implementation-facts-travel-with-the-branch-that-produced-them). That is most of (c).
· A design is already named by an id that resolves to a location, never by its path (rule:a-design-is-named-by-an-id-not-a-path). (b) extends the same rule to implementations.
· A real run can be fed back by file (chg:a-real-run-is-fed-back-by-file), and reflow2's own loop first closed on 2026-09-23.

PUSHBACK, recorded beside it:
· 🛑 OUT-OF-TREE FILES ARE ALREADY MEASURED INCONSISTENTLY. A file registered in another repository reads "unmeasurable — outside_root" locally and "missing_artifact — FAIL" in CI (fact:an-out-of-tree-artifact-registration-passed-locally-as-unmeasurable-and-failed-ci-as-missing). Today that is an edge case. After separation it is EVERY file, so it has to be settled first.
· PATHS DIFFER PER MACHINE. The design must never hold an absolute path; the per-machine half belongs in machine-local configuration, the way the dev_reflow2 hub's .mcp.json already holds each child's folder.
· WHICH BRANCH OF THE CODE does the design describe? The branch-overlay work (dec:how-a-branchs-implementation-facts-are-held) answers this for one repository; across a repository boundary, the implementation's branch has to be named too.
· ONE DESIGN, SEVERAL IMPLEMENTATIONS. cure is the example: its own MCP server and its own connector server may well be two repositories realizing one design. (b) handles that; (a) scatters it across every file.

THE FIRST REAL CASE: cure. Its design moves to flo2.io, shared with Anthony's sister and uncle; its code will be on Anthony's laptop. When implementation starts, an agent needs the design (via api.flo2.io), the code (a local checkout), and this link between them.

Idea is Anthony's; options, existing pieces and pushback are Claude Code's.
